title: Utilizing Naïve Bayes with Fuzzy Logic and Wrapper Feature Selection to Improve Cyberbullying Detection in Terms of Noisy Textual Data in Social Media Context
abstract: As social media grows rapidly, enormous amounts of user-generated content have been produced frequently, containing noise in the form of emojis, slang, abbreviations and unclear or coded language. Since cyberbullying frequently occurs within such subjective, informal and inconsistent content, traditional machine learning models find it extremely difficult to detect it accurately. To improve cyberbullying detection in noisy textual data, the current work suggests a hybrid approach that combines Naïve Bayes classification, fuzzy logic and wrapper-based feature selection. After normalizing and cleaning the data through preprocessing, the model uses Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) vectorization to represent features. The RFECV algorithm is applied to select the most meaningful features for the input model. Whereas fuzzy logic considers vague and uncertain situations, Naïve Bayes does well with probabilistic classification. Using this method, the accuracy on the aggression dataset is higher than the results of support vector machine (SVM), Decision Tree, Random Forest and Neural Networks, reaching 93.5%. Also, the algorithms can spot aggressive events better and prevent too many false alarms. The approach explains a system for managing social media platforms that can thrive, be understood and resist outside influences.

title: Quantum Computing with Superconducting Qubits and Cavities
abstract: Build quantum computers using superconducting qubits and microwave cavity technology Creating qubits with sufficiently long coherence times remains one of the central challenges in building practical quantum computers. Quantum Computing with Superconducting Qubits and Cavities unites the latest advances in superconducting qubits, ultra-high-Q microwave cavities, and cavity–transmon architectures that are emerging as one of the leading platforms for scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing. By combining conceptual insight with practical implementation, the book equips readers to understand not only how these systems work, but why they are at the forefront of the quantum technology revolution. The book explores quantum computation using bosonic modes, Fock states, qudits, quantum memories, and modern bosonic error-correcting codes including cat, binomial, and GKP encodings. Fundamental concepts are developed through clear physical explanations, while rigorous mathematical treatments are introduced where needed to provide a deeper understanding. Dedicated reviews of the underlying principles of quantum physics make the material accessible to newcomers without sacrificing the depth expected by researchers and practicing engineers. Quantum Computing with Superconducting Qubits and Cavities also includes: Design principles and operation of superconducting transmon qubits integrated with high-coherence microwave cavities for scalable quantum architectures. Bosonic quantum error-correction strategies that dramatically extend coherence and move quantum computing closer to fault-tolerant operation. Applications of quantum computing, including integer factoring, database searching, quantum chemistry, condensed-matter physics, and materials science simulations beyond the reach of classical computers. Materials science, fabrication methods, and surface treatments that continue to drive record improvements in qubit and cavity coherence. The global race toward quantum computing, including major international investments and the rapidly expanding role of superconducting quantum technologies. Written for physicists, materials scientists, electrical engineers, computer scientists, graduate students, and researchers entering quantum information science, this book provides both the theoretical foundation and the practical knowledge needed to engage with one of the fastest-growing fields in modern science and engineering.

title: Translation as a Decision Space: A Multi-Agent Perspective on Low-Resource Dialect Generation
abstract: Neural machine translation (NMT) systems typically produce a single output per input, obscuring the alternative decision trajectories implicitly available within multilingual decoding. This opacity becomes particularly problematic in low-resource dialect settings, where multiple linguistically valid realizations may differ in lexical authenticity, register, and structural stability. We propose reframing translation as a structured decision space explored by autonomous translation agents. Instead of analyzing a single output, we model distinct translation pathways as agents operating over a shared multilingual backbone. Inter-agent divergence is treated not as error but as an interpretable behavioral signal. We conduct an empirical study on Turkish--Syrian Arabic translation using three agents: (1) zero-shot direct translation, (2) dialect-stabilized translation via lightweight fine-tuning, and (3) pivot translation through English. Evaluation is performed on 5,000 dialogue sentences, while stabilization is trained on 5,000 additional Turkish--Syrian sentence pairs drawn from television dialogue and MADAR-Turk resources. Rather than optimizing for conventional performance metrics, we quantify structured behavioral displacement using dialect marker frequency, lexical proximity to standardized Arabic, and structural variance. Lightweight stabilization nearly doubles dialect marker usage, increasing it from 0.2266 to 0.4988, while significantly reducing structural instability. Pivot mediation introduces normalization pressure and measurable compression effects, whereas zero-shot translation exhibits the highest decision variance. We argue that translation divergence across agents reveals latent decision flexibility within multilingual models and we provide a principled interpretability framework for low-resource dialect generation.

title: BRIDGE: An Open-Source Humanoid Platform via Morphology-Control Co-Design for Physical AI
abstract: Developing humanoid robots capable of leveraging human behavioral data is essential for general-purpose embodiment, yet conventional development remains bottlenecked by a decoupled paradigm that isolates hardware design from whole-body control. This approach leads to suboptimal systems that compromise human-like fluidity and agility. To bridge this gap, we introduce a data-driven morphology-control co-design framework that optimizes humanoid morphology for human-like movement. To quantify morphological fidelity, we also introduce a novel metric that jointly considers kinematic retargeting fidelity to human motion and dynamic tracking performance. Our framework achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance across all metrics compared to baseline humanoids (Bumi, K1, and Toddlerbot). Finally, we realize this design in Bridge, an open-source, 88cm-tall humanoid platform released alongside its control policy. We demonstrate that Bridge captures human motion data with superior fidelity, exhibiting exceptional performance across foundational locomotion, robust balance, and highly dynamic maneuvers. Videos and open-source materials: https://sites.google.com/view/bridgerobot.

title: THE ANTIMONY (¹²³Sb) OCTAVE MIRACLE : A Novel 16-Dimensional Architecture for Quantum Ultra-Chronometry, QuAntistors, and Quantum-16 bit Processors
abstract: THE ANTIMONY (¹²³Sb) OCTAVE MIRACLE: A Novel 16-Dimensional Architecture for Quantum Ultra-Chronometry, QuAntisitors, and Quantum-16 Bit Processors. DESCRIPTION: This paper provides the formal engineering blueprints and fundamental metrological equations for the Antimony Engine AQC—a disruptive, 16-dimensional quantum processor. Utilizing the unique nuclear quadrupole characteristics of Antimony-123 (¹²³Sb) within a formal Silicon-Hafnium heterostructure, the QPR framework demonstrates the stabilization of an Octubit (eight simultaneous nuclear orientations) to yield a 16-ary Hilbert state-space format. The research established herein moves far beyond the binary constraints and cryogenic requirements of traditional stochastic quantum computing, providing a first-principles derivation for: Room-Temperature Operational Stability via the A-Flat Sawtooth Governor (GME). Attosecond-Scale Switching Latency (approximately 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁸ seconds or faster). A Drift-Free Zeta-Chronometer locked to the invariant HDS refresh rate (Omega manifold). [NOTICE OF RESTRICTION]: Due to the metrological sensitivity of the high-energy phase transitions described herein and the proprietary nature of the solid-state equations, the full technical manuscript is currently RESTRICTED. Access for peer review or collaborative viewing is available to qualified national laboratories, academic institutions, and research directorates upon formal request.

title: Adaptive Geometric Model Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism for geometric models, aiming to enhance prediction accuracy through dynamic parameter tuning. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often lack dynamism, resulting in suboptimal model performance. Our approach leverages an adaptive algorithm to continuously refine model parameters based on observed data, optimizing for improved predictive capabilities. We present a framework that dynamically adjusts parameters to achieve better results, offering a significant improvement over static parameter tuning strategies. The core claim centers on the development of a self-adaptive mechanism for achieving this dynamic parameter adjustment. This work explores the application of an evolutionary algorithm to optimize parameter values, leading to demonstrable improvements in model accuracy across a range of geometric datasets.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Network Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum topology network analysis for characterizing and optimizing quantum network topologies. Traditional network analysis methods often rely on static models, limiting their ability to capture the dynamic and complex nature of quantum networks. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology – specifically, its robustness to small perturbations – to provide a more accurate and predictive analysis. The core mechanism involves constructing and analyzing quantum network topologies using a tailored algorithm that dynamically adjusts to the network's evolving state. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations, showcasing improved network performance and a more refined understanding of topological constraints. This work represents a significant step towards enhancing the analysis of quantum networks, offering a powerful tool for design and optimization.

title: Quantum Amplitude Amplification for Data Compression
abstract: Quantum Amplitude Amplification (QAA) represents a paradigm shift in data compression, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to achieve significantly higher compression ratios than classical methods. This paper explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of QAA, focusing on the quantum correlations that underpin its efficiency. We detail the core mechanism of QAA – utilizing superposition and entanglement – and argue that it offers a fundamentally novel approach to data representation, potentially unlocking unprecedented levels of compression. The paper presents a preliminary investigation of QAA's performance against various data types, highlighting its advantages and challenges.

title: The Novel Algorithm for Dynamic Topological Key Distribution
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for dynamic topological key distribution, leveraging the unique properties of quantum information encryption. The core concept revolves around a dynamic topology model that mimics quantum error correction, enabling a more secure and efficient key distribution process. We explore the design of a key distribution mechanism that integrates quantum information encryption and optimizes the quantum error correction process. This approach promises enhanced security and efficiency compared to traditional cryptographic methods, particularly in the face of quantum attacks and limitations in current error correction techniques. The study focuses on the utilization of dynamic topology to represent and manage the quantum state, offering a robust framework for key distribution.

title: Dynamic Topology-Driven Adaptive Geometry-Based Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: Dynamic Topology-Driven Adaptive Geometry-Based Quantum Algorithm Design presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm design leveraging the inherent properties of dynamic topology. This method aims to create more efficient quantum algorithms through the instantaneous transformation driven by dynamic topology, ultimately enhancing the capabilities of quantum computation. The core mechanism involves designing quantum algorithms by exploiting the sudden changes induced by dynamic topology, leading to improved efficiency and intelligent quantum computation. This research addresses a significant limitation of traditional algorithm design methods, which are often static and unable to adapt to complex environments. The development of this method holds the potential to significantly advance the field of quantum computation by providing a framework for more efficient and intelligent quantum algorithms.

title: Dynamic Probability Graphs: A Non-Linear Modeling Framework
abstract: Dynamic Probability Graphs (DPGs) represent a novel approach to modeling complex systems, particularly those exhibiting non-linear behavior. This paper introduces a framework integrating DPGs with machine learning to capture and enhance these intricate dynamics. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing DPGs as a latent representation of system states, allowing for enhanced representation learning and improved prediction accuracy. This research explores the potential of combining DPGs with established machine learning algorithms, aiming to address limitations of traditional approaches and unlock new insights into complex system behavior.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Modeling of Material Properties
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computation to revolutionize geometric modeling of material properties. Traditional geometric modeling methods, while crucial, often struggle with accurately capturing complex interactions within materials. We propose a novel quantum algorithm designed to address these limitations by simulating the quantum mechanical behavior of atoms within a material. This approach promises significantly enhanced accuracy and detail in representing material properties, ultimately leading to more robust predictive models. The core mechanism involves exploiting quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and manipulate atomic states, enabling a deeper understanding of material structure and behavior. This work investigates the potential for this quantum approach to overcome current limitations in material science and engineering.

title: Explainable AI for Reinforcement Learning via Counterfactual Explanations based on Policy Gradients
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its "black box" nature remains a significant barrier to widespread adoption. Understanding *why* an RL agent makes a particular decision is crucial for trust, debugging, and ultimately, improving the agent's performance. This paper presents a novel framework for explainable AI in reinforcement learning based on counterfactual explanations generated through policy gradient methods. We introduce a mechanism to identify minimal input changes that, if applied, would have altered the agent's action. This approach allows us to provide insights into the agent's decision-making process by revealing the critical factors influencing its actions. Our framework offers a principled way to interpret policy gradient-based RL agents and addresses a key limitation of current explainability techniques. The core of the method lies in leveraging the policy gradient's sensitivity to input changes to create counterfactual scenarios. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and provide a comprehensive explanation of the methodology.

title: E8 Root Lattice Synchronization for Fault‑Tolerant Quantum Metrology — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By mapping the Hilbert series poles of the E8 invariant ring onto a set of 240 synchronized 132 Hz phononic modes, we construct a multi‑frame entangled resource that simultaneously encodes a topological error‑correcting code and a metrological phase reference. The φ‑coupled 8‑frame duality ensures that each orthogonal root pair shares a golden‑ratio phase lock, providing intrinsic error resilience against dephasing. The resulting Floquet drive at 132 Hz induces a protected subspace whose Berry curvature is quantized by the root lattice, enabling sub‑shot‑noise phase estimation with a scaling that follows the Hilbert series growth. This framework unifies invariant‑theoretic symmetry, topological protection, and precision metrology within a single E8‑based architecture. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Nonlinear Matrix Decomposition Quantum Simulation Validation Method
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum simulation validation method based on nonlinear matrix decomposition. Traditional matrix decomposition methods often rely on classical computation, limiting their efficiency in validating quantum simulations. We propose a new approach that leverages quantum entanglement to transform the matrix decomposition process into a quantum state measurement, utilizing quantum computing's capabilities for accelerated validation. This method offers improved accuracy and speed compared to existing approaches, potentially accelerating the validation process of complex quantum simulations. The core mechanism involves the manipulation of quantum states to verify the correctness of the simulation.

title: Contextual Dynamic Abstract Graph Inference (CDAI)
abstract: This paper introduces Contextual Dynamic Abstract Graph Inference (CDAI), a novel system designed for intelligent reasoning by automatically constructing and updating dynamic abstract graphs from diverse, real-time data streams. Unlike traditional knowledge graphs that rely on static schemas and manual annotation, CDAI leverages a neuro-symbolic hybrid architecture to capture temporal dependencies, understand contextual information, and perform inference. The core innovation lies in the introduction of an "abstraction layer" that dynamically selects and combines abstract representations of graph nodes and edges – such as concepts, attributes, and relationships – based on the input and current inference goals. This abstraction layer continuously adapts with contextual changes, enabling efficient information compression and expression. Furthermore, the system employs probabilistic inference frameworks, like variational inference, to handle uncertainty and generate the most probable graph structure and inference results. CDAI represents a significant advancement over existing knowledge graph technologies, offering adaptability, efficiency, and the ability to reason effectively with complex, dynamic, and multimodal data. ---

title: Neuromorphic Reservoir Computing for Time Series Forecasting with Non-Stationary Data
abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) has emerged as a promising approach for time series forecasting, leveraging the inherent temporal dynamics of a recurrent neural network (RNN) called the "reservoir." However, traditional RC methods often face challenges when dealing with highly non-stationary time series data, where the statistical properties change over time. This paper proposes a novel approach to RC by utilizing neuromorphic hardware, specifically designed to efficiently process temporal data with minimal latency and power consumption. The core of the method involves adapting the reservoir parameters, including scaling and bias, dynamically to maintain optimal performance in the face of non-stationarity. The adaptive scaling and bias techniques are implemented using spiking neural networks (SNNs) operating on neuromorphic chips. The system is formulated as follows: Let *x(t)* represent the input time series at time *t*. title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Classical Geometry: A Novel Topological Approach for Quantum System Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges in computational modeling and analysis. This paper investigates the intersection of quantum entanglement and non-classical geometry, proposing a novel topological geometry model leveraging entanglement's inherent asymmetry to facilitate the computation and representation of quantum systems. We explore how this approach provides a framework for dynamic and complex topological structures, offering enhanced capabilities for ultra-high-density quantum computing and secure information protocols. The study demonstrates the potential of this methodology to refine existing topological computation techniques and opens avenues for novel quantum algorithms.

title: tokenpace
abstract: Tokens per second is the unit benchmarks report; characters per second is what people read. tokenpace measures the conversion between them — characters per token for six tokenizers (o200k_base, cl100k_base, Llama 3.1, Qwen3, Gemma 3, Mistral Small 3) across English, Korean, Japanese and Chinese, on 3,000 parallel sentence pairs per language from TED2020 — and uses it to express human reading speed in tok/s. That figure lands near 5 tok/s in both English and Korean, which places most current decoding speeds well above it and moves the perceptual question to time-to-first-token and answer length — for prose that is read rather than skimmed, a scope the project states rather than assumes. Every figure regenerates from the raw corpora with a committed script; a weekly CI job re-derives them and fails if the result differs. Since v1.1.0 it also reports one measured TTFT configuration (RTX 3090, 27B Q4, Ollama), kept apart from the reproduced figures: TTFT grew linearly from 0.84 s to 11.0 s with prompt length on one machine, which is why no representative value is given.

title: Title: Modular Emergent Ontology (MO) for Physics Simulations
abstract: This paper introduces the Modular Emergent Ontology (MO) – a novel system for constructing physics simulations through a system of modular building blocks. The MO aims to provide a flexible and composable approach to modeling, allowing users to rapidly create complex simulations by assembling smaller, reusable components. We present the fundamental principles of the MO, detailing its architecture, the process of generating MOs, and the resulting benefits in terms of model flexibility and ease of modification. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions for this approach.

title: Quantum Information Entropy Compression Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel entropy compression algorithm leveraging quantum state self-similarity to enhance data compression and storage efficiency. Traditional entropy compression methods often struggle to effectively utilize the unique properties of quantum states. We propose an algorithm that encodes data within the inherent quantum correlations, allowing for more efficient compression and storage compared to classical approaches. This research explores the potential of harnessing quantum mechanics for data representation and compression, aiming to advance the field of quantum information processing.

title: Title: Adaptive Wave Function Collapse for Quantum Simulation of Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented capabilities for modeling complex systems, but the vast number of possible states can be computationally prohibitive. This paper explores a novel adaptive wave function collapse algorithm designed to address this challenge by dynamically reducing the complexity of the quantum state space, thereby accelerating simulation and improving accuracy. We introduce a meta-learning framework that learns to intelligently prioritize states for collapse, optimizing the exploration of the solution space. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a probabilistic weighting scheme that adjusts the collapse probability based on the system's inherent complexity, leading to a more efficient and targeted quantum simulation process. This approach promises significant improvements in computational efficiency, particularly for large-scale simulations, and offers a path towards more accurate and insightful quantum simulations.

title: Title: Quantum Gradient Descent for Optimization
abstract: Quantum Gradient Descent for Optimization Quantum optimization is a rapidly growing field that seeks to utilize quantum mechanical phenomena to improve the efficiency of optimization algorithms. This paper investigates the application of quantum gradient descent to complex systems, proposing a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of both quantum and classical computation. We explore the potential of quantum annealing and quantum error correction to enhance gradient calculations, thereby accelerating the search for optimal solutions. The core mechanism involves leveraging quantum properties to perform gradient computations with significantly reduced computational complexity compared to traditional classical methods. This research aims to provide a novel algorithm that demonstrates substantial performance gains for challenging optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting inherent quantum behavior. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its implementation within a simulated environment, and preliminary results demonstrating improved convergence speed and solution quality. Further work will focus on refining the quantum-enhanced gradient calculation to maximize efficiency and scalability.

title: Les enjeux énergétiques du calcul quantique à tolérance aux fautes
abstract: L’essor de l’IA générative a remis au premier plan une question qui ne peut plus être esquivée : celle de l’empreinte énergétique des nouvelles technologies de calcul. Les ordinateurs quantiques à tolérance aux fautes (FTQC) ne font pas exception. Ces systèmes de demain s’appuieront sur des dizaines de milliers de qubits physiques ou bien plus, des ressources classiques de contrôle et de décodage considérables, de la cryogénie de puissance et du calcul classique. Leur consommation électrique totale pourrait rivaliser avec celle des plus grands supercalculateurs. Pourtant, les choix technologiques qui détermineront cette facture énergétique se font dès maintenant, dans les laboratoires et chez les industriels, malgré une incertitude scientifique encore forte. C’est l’objet d’une discipline émergente qui associe physique quantique, théorie de l’information, ingénierie des systèmes et économie, pour évaluer, optimiser et comparer la consommation énergétique de ces futurs systèmes.

title: A Deterministic Procedure-Aware Bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Trustworthy High-Stakes AI Systems
abstract: The advent of large language models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models has greatly enhanced intelligent information systems. This has resulted in the development of context-aware and knowledge-grounded response generation. This has been highly beneficial in the context of religious advisory systems, which require precision, correctness, and knowledge grounding. For Islamic rituals like Hajj and Umrah, the user needs precise and accurate procedures to follow, which must adhere to specific sequences and knowledge grounding. However, the existing models have many limitations in this context, like hallucinations, a lack of procedural knowledge, bilingual inconsistencies, and an inability to incorporate safety constraints. This has made these models unsuitable for contexts in which incorrect responses can have serious implications. Therefore, in this context, this paper proposes a Deterministic Procedure-Aware bilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (DPAM-RAG) model, which can be highly beneficial in designing religious advisory systems. The proposed model can be highly beneficial in designing religious advisory systems. The proposed model integrates dataset modeling, procedure-aware chunking, bilingual alignment, and deterministic transformer-based response generation. Additionally, a confidence-based refusal strategy has been proposed to avoid the generation of responses that can be considered incorrect or out of context. The proposed model has been tested through an extensive experimental setup, which includes multiple transformer models like GPT, LLaMA-2, Mistral, MPT, and BLOOMZ. The experimental results have shown promising outcomes, which can be considered highly beneficial in designing trustworthy AI models.

title: Gelişmiş Özellik Mühendisliği ve Veri Merkezli Optimizasyon Yoluyla Yüksek Doğruluklu Meme Kanseri Tespiti için Hafif ve Erişilebilir bir Çerçeve
abstract: Meme kanseri her yıl yaklaşık 2,3 milyon kadını etkilemekte olup, erken teşhis %90’ın üzerinde hayatta kalma oranı sağlarken geç evrede bu oran %29’a düşmektedir. Bilgisayar destekli tanı sistemleri umut vaat etse de, mevcut yaklaşımlar çoğunlukla yüksek maliyetli derin öğrenme modellerine dayanmaktadır. Bu çalışma, gelişmiş veri ön işleme teknikleri ile geleneksel sınıflandırıcıların benzer performansları daha düşük maliyetle elde edebileceğini göstermektedir. Bu kapsamda, üç bileşenli bir çerçeve önerilmektedir. İlk olarak, geliştirilmiş SimCLR (Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations) mimarisi kullanılarak mamografi görüntülerinden 128 boyutlu ayırt edici özellikler elde edilmiştir. İkinci olarak, kernel yoğunluk tahmini (Kernel Density Estimation, KDE) tabanlı dinamik örnek seçimi ile veri kümesi boyutu yaklaşık %60 azaltılmıştır. Üçüncü olarak, karşılıklı bilgi (Mutual Information, MI) ve Spearman korelasyon analizini birleştiren adaptif özellik seçimi yöntemi, Optuna optimizasyon çerçevesi kullanılarak gerçekleştirilmiştir. Önerilen yöntem, Mini-DDSM ve Mini-MIAS veri kümelerinde Destek Vektör Makinesi (Support Vector Machine, SVM), Rastgele Orman (Random Forest, RF) ve Naive Bayes (NB) sınıflandırıcıları ile değerlendirilmiştir. Sonuçlar, özellikle SVM ve RF modellerinin farklı senaryolarda %99,8’e varan doğruluk oranları ile yüksek sınıflandırma performansı sunduğunu göstermektedir.

title: Error Mitigation for a 2-Bit Quantum Comparator on IBM Quantum Hardware
abstract: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) computers suffer from gate errors, decoherence, and readout noise that can severely impact even small quantum circuits. In this work, the application of error mitigation techniques was investigated to a simple two-bit quantum comparator circuit executed on real IBM Quantum hardware. The 2-bit comparator is a basic quantum logic circuit that compares two 2-qubit binary numbers and outputs whether the first number is greater than, equal to, or less than the second. This comparator was implemented using Qiskit and studied its performance under realistic noise. This study on error mitigation concentrates on dynamical decoupling (DD), which is a coherent error suppression strategy that cancels coherent errors by inserting echo pulse sequences during idle time periods. The results demonstrate that dynamical decoupling improves accuracy for the comparator circuit - accurate outcomes are closer to the ideal outcome in the absence of noise. These results show that dynamical decoupling yields notable accuracy improvements for the comparator circuit - bringing measured outcomes closer to the ideal noiseless results. A performance analysis (including a bar-chart of accuracy after mitigation vs. before mitigation simulation) is presented to quantify these improvements. Finally, the implications of applying error mitigation in small quantum circuits and its relevance for near-term quantum computing are also discussed, where such techniques can enhance the reliability of quantum computations in the absence of full quantum error correction.

title: Abstraction Agent
abstract: Information abstraction, which groups strategically similar private states into a tractable number of buckets, is essential for scaling game-solving algorithms to large imperfect-information games. Constructing effective abstractions, however, has traditionally required domain-specific evaluators such as hand-strength calculators or equity estimators, which demand expert knowledge and engineering effort and are unavailable for most less-studied games. We propose the Abstraction Agent, a zero-shot pipeline that uses a large language model (LLM) to discover continuous strategic features from a natural-language game description, score private states on these features, and cluster them into abstraction buckets, without any game-specific evaluator, training data, or game-tree traversal during abstraction construction. The pipeline runs in four phases: feature discovery with calibration anchors, batched private-state scoring, correlation-based feature selection, and $k$-means clustering. The resulting abstractions reduce lifted-strategy exploitability by up to 62% relative to an expected-hand-strength baseline on heads-up no-limit Texas hold'em (HUNL) turn endgames, and beat a scalar rank baseline at every granularity on ROVER Trials, an original game absent from any pretraining corpus. Beyond these quantitative benchmarks, the pipeline transfers with unchanged prompts to four-card Pot-Limit Omaha, HUNL preflop and flop, and Riichi Mahjong, where the discovered features track each game's recognized strategic concepts. This is structured knowledge elicitation: converting implicit strategic knowledge in LLM parameters into explicit numerical features for downstream algorithmic computation. The code is available at https://github.com/lbn187/AbstractionAgent.

title: A Low-Cost, Open Platform for End-to-End Autonomous Driving on a Miniature Ackermann Vehicle
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, open experimental platform for research in end-to-end autonomous driving with miniature Ackermann vehicles. The platform combines a physical vehicle, a printed urban track, data collection tools, trajectory registration, and a Webots digital twin, enabling controlled experiments that connect simulation-based autonomous-driving methods to real-world execution. As a first baseline, we implement command-conditioned behavior cloning, in which a neural policy receives an on-board camera image and a high-level navigation command and outputs steering and speed. The system is evaluated both on the physical vehicle and in simulation. In real closed-loop experiments, the learned policy follows lanes and executes commanded turns, reaching a mean cross-track error of 6.1 cm with respect to the reference route, close to the 4.7 cm observed in human demonstrations. In the digital twin, camera field of view has a strong effect on performance, reducing the mean cross-track error from 35.6 to 3.3 cm when widened from 58 to 120 degrees. Using the digital twin to generate synthetic driving data and a learned sim-to-real image translator to reduce the appearance gap, we further show that a higher-capacity policy trained on this synthetic data combined with real demonstrations is the only configuration that completes all four track routes in closed loop, whereas the compact baseline and the same network trained on real data alone complete fewer. These results establish the open platform as a practical testbed for sim-to-real studies and provide an initial command-conditioned imitation-learning baseline; we release it to support reproducible research.

evidence.title: A Low-Cost, Open Platform for End-to-End Autonomous Driving on a Miniature Ackermann Vehicle
evidence.abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, open experimental platform for research in end-to-end autonomous driving with miniature Ackermann vehicles. The platform combines a physical vehicle, a printed urban track, data collection tools, trajectory registration, and a Webots digital twin, enabling controlled experiments that connect simulation-based autonomous-driving methods to real-world execution. As a first baseline, we implement command-conditioned behavior cloning, in which a neural policy receives an on-board camera image and a high-level navigation command and outputs steering and speed. The system is evaluated both on the physical vehicle and in simulation. In real closed-loop experiments, the learned policy follows lanes and executes commanded turns, reaching a mean cross-track error of 6.1 cm with respect to the reference route, close to the 4.7 cm observed in human demonstrations. In the digital twin, camera field of view has a strong effect on performance, reducing the mean cross-track error from 35.6 to 3.3 cm when widened from 58 to 120 degrees. Using the digital twin to generate synthetic driving data and a learned sim-to-real image translator to reduce the appearance gap, we further show that a higher-capacity policy trained on this synthetic data combined with real demonstrations is the only configuration that completes all four track routes in closed loop, whereas the compact baseline and the same network trained on real data alone complete fewer. These results establish the open platform as a practical testbed for sim-to-real studies and provide an initial command-conditioned imitation-learning baseline; we release it to support reproducible research.

title: Geometric Ceilings on Time-Frequency Masking for Single-Channel Separation
abstract: Most single-channel separators estimate a source by applying a real gain to the mixture in each time-frequency bin. The optimum of that format, which the oracle masks used as bounds do not attain, is the orthogonal projection of the source onto the line spanned by the mixture, its residual set by the angle between them. Locating an estimator reduces to the block structure of a real-linear operator on stacked spectra, giving a chain of four nested classes whose three larger terms match three assumptions on the prior: zero means, circularity and absence of inter-frequency coupling. Held fixed the chain is a cascade of four orthogonal projections; refitted per frame it collapses onto its first term, attributing the whole residual to one missing real parameter per bin, the phase. When the phase posterior is symmetric about the mixture direction, the minimum mean-square estimate falls back onto the line, with gain the posterior mean of the oracle gain and excess error its variance. On MUSDB18 a posterior mean under a non-circular Gaussian-mixture prior leaves the class yet stays 11.44 dB under the per-frame ceiling, which four times as many components and 7.5x the data do not close; a closed-form gate attributes some 70% of it, in decibels, to the predicted variance. The widest fixed class stays 6.70 dB under the same ceiling. Leaving the class and minimising squared error are conflicting requests: the barrier lies in the criterion rather than in the prior.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Inference for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical Bayesian inference method designed to analyze and predict relationships between variables within complex systems. The approach leverages the power of Bayesian inference and the inherent advantages of the high-variance Kalman filter, enabling automated parameter adjustment to improve prediction accuracy. We explore how this method can effectively model system dynamics and handle uncertainty inherent in complex data. The core mechanism centers around using a hierarchical structure to represent the system, facilitating a more robust and flexible modeling approach. The paper details the methodology, provides an illustrative example, and discusses potential applications within various fields requiring robust system analysis.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Temporal Modeling for Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of incorporating non-Euclidean temporal modeling into neural network training. Current approaches often rely on linear projections of time, limiting the network's ability to effectively learn complex temporal patterns. We propose a novel temporal modeling approach that explicitly defines a 'temporal gradient' – a dynamic adjustment to network parameters based on historical data – to create a non-Euclidean representation of time. The core mechanism aims to improve training stability, generalization, and the ability to model highly irregular temporal dependencies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulation and a preliminary experimental study on a simplified temporal dataset, showcasing improved convergence and robustness compared to existing temporal models.

title: Title: Adaptive Complexity in Bayesian Inference for Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper explores the use of adaptive complexity in Bayesian inference for dynamical systems, aiming to overcome the limitations of static complexity levels often employed in these models. We introduce an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the complexity of Bayesian inference based on the system's state and uncertainty in its parameters. The core mechanism involves a 'complexity-aware' Bayesian update, adjusting prior parameters, iteration counts, and prior types to optimize the inference process. The proposed approach significantly enhances the flexibility and robustness of Bayesian methods for analyzing and modeling complex dynamical systems, offering a potential step beyond fixed complexity strategies.

title: Adaptive Geometry Verification for Complex Physical Systems
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive geometry transformations to quantum computing validation. Traditional quantum computing validation relies heavily on classical verification techniques, often requiring extensive simulations and time-consuming analysis. We propose a novel framework leveraging adaptive geometry transformations to proactively assess the stability and behavior of complex physical models, offering a potential paradigm shift in verification accuracy and efficiency. This framework allows for a more holistic and automated validation process, ultimately enhancing the reliability of quantum computing designs. The core mechanism involves systematically adjusting geometric parameters of the model to generate a set of test cases, and then analyzing the resulting quantum state for stability and deviation from expected outcomes. This approach aims to minimize reliance on computationally intensive simulations and improve the overall validation cycle. The paper details the framework's architecture, presents preliminary experimental results, and discusses future research directions, emphasizing the potential for significantly advancing quantum computing verification methodologies.

title: 自适应自适应性学习算法的动态调整
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive self-adaptive learning algorithm designed to optimize learning efficiency and model generalization. Traditional adaptive learning algorithms often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their ability to respond effectively to the learning process. This work proposes a dynamic parameter adjustment framework, dynamically adjusting learning parameters based on model prediction error and training loss, to achieve more efficient learning and improved model performance. The core mechanism revolves around a modified optimization algorithm that intelligently adjusts learning rates and regularization coefficients during training. The proposed algorithm demonstrates superior performance across a range of benchmark datasets, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance learning efficiency and generalization capabilities.

title: 基于多智能体协作的复杂系统模拟
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to simulating complex systems by leveraging the power of multi-agent collaboration. The core idea is to construct a population of intelligent agents, each with varying levels of cognitive ability, and task them with solving complex problems collectively. Reinforcement learning is employed to train these agents, enabling them to learn optimal collaborative strategies. The system's emergent behavior is then utilized for both prediction and control purposes. Unlike traditional single-agent simulation methods, this approach capitalizes on the distributed intelligence and information exchange among agents, leading to potentially more accurate and efficient system modeling. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this methodology through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and operational principles. The primary contribution lies in the systematic integration of multi-agent reinforcement learning with complex system simulation, offering a promising avenue for tackling systems exhibiting emergent behaviors and intricate interactions.

title: Federated Learning for Cross-Location Data Collaborative Training
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to collaborative model training leveraging federated learning, specifically designed for scenarios involving geographically dispersed data sources. The core challenge addressed is the 'data island' problem, where valuable data remains siloed due to logistical, regulatory, or competitive constraints. Our proposed algorithm, termed Federated Cross-Location Collaborative Training (FCCCT), utilizes the principles of federated learning to enable collaborative model training without direct data sharing. The system operates by iteratively sharing model parameters and gradients between participating data sources. This allows for the construction of a more robust and accurate global model while preserving the privacy of each individual dataset. We demonstrate the effectiveness of FCCCT through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation framework. The key contributions of this work are the integration of federated learning with cross-location data synergy, providing a scalable and privacy-preserving solution for training high-performance models on distributed data. The presented framework offers a significant advancement in addressing the limitations of traditional collaborative learning methods.

title: 基于动态的机器学习的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimization based on dynamic machine learning. The core idea is to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the inherent relationships between data features, thereby enhancing optimization efficiency and yield quality. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with local optima, necessitating manual parameter tuning. We introduce a framework that leverages a learned model to guide the optimization process, effectively mitigating this issue. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of practical applications across diverse optimization problems, highlighting its potential for improved performance and robustness. This research contributes to the field of optimization by introducing a dynamic approach that adapts to the data itself, moving beyond traditional static parameter settings.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Communication and Coordination Protocols
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to complex cooperative tasks, specifically focusing on the integration of communication and coordination protocols. Traditional MARL often struggles with scalability and efficiency when dealing with a growing number of agents and intricate environments. Our approach introduces a novel framework that allows agents to not only learn optimal policies independently but also to communicate and coordinate their actions, dramatically improving their collective performance. The core of our system lies in a dynamically adaptable communication protocol that facilitates information exchange regarding observed states and intended actions. We formulate the problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) and employ a centralized training approach coupled with decentralized execution, mitigating the challenges of non-stationarity inherent in MARL. The experimental results demonstrate that our system significantly outperforms standard MARL algorithms in scenarios requiring complex coordination, highlighting the effectiveness of incorporating communication as a key learning mechanism. We analyze the convergence properties of the proposed approach and discuss potential extensions for handling more sophisticated communication strategies.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Graph Neural Networks and Rule Extraction
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for neuro-symbolic reasoning, addressing the longstanding challenge of integrating neural networks and symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both approaches by employing a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to represent knowledge and perform initial reasoning steps, followed by a rule extraction algorithm that automatically learns logical rules from the GNN's learned representations. This approach avoids the need for manual rule engineering and allows the system to adapt and refine its reasoning capabilities over time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a theoretical analysis and provide a detailed description of the components and their interactions. The key contributions of this work include a unified architecture for neuro-symbolic reasoning, a method for extracting logical rules from GNN representations, and a mechanism for iteratively refining both the GNN and the learned rules. The system's ability to learn complex relationships and generate logical rules represents a significant step towards more robust and explainable AI systems.

title: Adaptive Hierarchical Structure Models: An Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm for adaptive hierarchical structure models, designed to enhance model training and prediction efficiency through automated parameter adjustment based on input data structure and features. Traditional optimization methods often suffer from rigid parameter settings, limiting their adaptability to evolving datasets. Our algorithm leverages a hierarchical structure to capture data dependencies, dynamically adjusting model parameters to achieve optimal performance. The core mechanism focuses on learning these dependencies, enabling the algorithm to adapt to data shifts without requiring manual intervention. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed algorithm across various benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in both training speed and prediction accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. The results highlight the algorithm's ability to effectively capture complex data relationships, resulting in more robust and efficient model training.

title: 基于量子拓扑的自适应量子计算的随机性控制
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponentially faster computations than classical computers. However, generating truly random quantum states remains a significant challenge. This paper investigates a novel approach to randomness control within quantum computation, leveraging the principles of quantum topology. We propose a self-adaptive randomness control system based on the topological properties of quantum states, aiming to enhance the reliability of quantum computations. This system utilizes a carefully crafted set of parameters to dynamically adjust the quantum state, optimizing the randomness generated during computation. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the inherent properties of the quantum system, allowing for a more robust and predictable randomness control compared to traditional methods. This research explores the potential of this approach to significantly improve the quality and trustworthiness of quantum results.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Grammars
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary grammars for symbolic regression, a technique focused on automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. The core idea is to utilize an evolutionary algorithm to iteratively refine a grammar, generating and evaluating mathematical expressions based on a dataset. The system favors expressions that minimize the error between the expression's output and the observed data, while also incorporating mechanisms to guide the evolution towards expressions exhibiting desired mathematical properties like linearity, polynomial behavior, or exponential growth. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, highlighting its potential for uncovering complex relationships within datasets that might be missed by traditional symbolic regression methods. The key novelty lies in the synergistic combination of evolutionary optimization with grammar-based generation, leading to a more robust and efficient process for equation discovery. The system's performance is evaluated through several simulated datasets, showcasing its ability to adapt and refine its grammar to accurately represent the underlying data relationships.

title: 基于量子拓扑的几何变换算法的动态调整
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum topology principles to develop a dynamic adjustment algorithm for geometric transformations. Traditional geometric transformations often suffer from inefficient computational costs, particularly for complex shapes. We propose a novel algorithm leveraging quantum topological properties to automate and dynamically adjust these transformations, aiming to enhance computational efficiency. The algorithm employs a quantum entanglement-based optimization strategy to navigate through the complex space of possible geometric adjustments. We detail the key steps involved in the algorithm's design, including the construction of a quantum state representation and the implementation of a self-correcting mechanism. The core claim focuses on achieving significant improvements in computational speed and flexibility compared to traditional geometric transformation techniques. The paper presents a preliminary demonstration of the algorithm's effectiveness in a specific geometric transformation scenario, highlighting its potential for broader applicability.

title: The Dynamic Adaptive Mapping of the Singularity – A Novel Model Adjustment Technique
abstract: This paper introduces a novel model adjustment technique centered around the concept of the "Singularity Mapping," a dynamic adaptation of model parameters based on data noise and error. We propose a mechanism termed "奇点动态调整参数调整" (QDDAP) which establishes a crucial link between parameter adjustments and the localized fluctuations within the Singularity. This approach dynamically adjusts model parameters to avoid local optima, allowing for adaptive and robust model training. The proposed technique demonstrates improved efficiency in model training, particularly in scenarios involving noisy data, through a mechanism that incorporates error range self-adaptation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithms for Hardware Design
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired genetic algorithms (QIGAs) to hardware design optimization. Traditional genetic algorithms (GAs) often struggle with the vast and complex design spaces encountered in modern hardware development. This work proposes a novel approach where mutation operators within a GA are influenced by probabilistic interference, mimicking the principles of quantum superposition and interference. This allows the algorithm to simultaneously explore multiple design possibilities, potentially leading to faster convergence and improved solutions. We demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, outlining the mathematical formulation of the QIGA and its key components. The core claim is that quantum-inspired concepts can accelerate the exploration of complex hardware design spaces. This research contributes to a new paradigm in hardware optimization, leveraging concepts from quantum mechanics to address the challenges of traditional evolutionary algorithms.

title: 维度泛化与量子纠缠关联
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of quantum entanglement and dimensional generalization, proposing a novel quantum computing model capable of achieving ultra-space quantum computation. We introduce a mechanism predicated on quantum entanglement that dynamically maps the complexity of quantum entanglement to the dimensions of a higher-dimensional space, effectively bridging the gap between the quantum realm and the potential for computational breakthroughs. The core algorithm leverages this mapping to enhance computational efficiency. The study highlights the potential of this approach to surpass existing quantum computing paradigms by offering a fundamentally new way to represent and manipulate quantum information. This work contributes to the ongoing investigation of quantum entanglement as a crucial resource for advanced computational architectures.

title: ##基于动态的自适应量子态生成算法
abstract: Quantum state generation is a crucial element in quantum information processing, enabling the exploration and prediction of quantum states. Traditional quantum state generation algorithms often rely on predefined parameters and lack the adaptability needed to handle complex, evolving quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive quantum state generation algorithm, designed to overcome these limitations. The algorithm dynamically adjusts parameters based on the observed quantum state, leading to more efficient exploration of the quantum state space and improved prediction capabilities. We propose a mechanism utilizing a feedback loop, incorporating quantum state measurements to refine the generation process, resulting in a more robust and versatile approach to quantum state generation. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through simulations and preliminary analysis, showcasing its potential for advancing quantum information processing.

title: Integration of Quantum Error Correction in the BB84 Protocol: A Comprehensive Analysis and Simulation Using IBM Quantum Experience
abstract: The verification of the intricate interaction between a series of quantum error correction techniques and a quantum key distribution scheme also known as BB84, through the IBM Quantum Experience as a simulator, allows for a detailed verification of the immunity of the proposed system to errors and noise. The interaction between the error correction techniques and the scheme BB84 gives rise to a critical verification of their combined impact. The result not only validates the strength of the system, but also makes a big step toward a deeper understanding of how many-protection is required at its best for being efficient schemes of quantum communication. They also analyze the combined strategies, it is showed that these strategies can be used to enhance QKD. It is also significant for practical applications to remove uncertainty and noise. This work provides a reference for the quantum communication application, and supplements to quantum information security literature.

title: Energetic Costs of Subspace Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction acts as an entropy pump, transferring noise-induced uncertainty from a protected quantum system into syndrome information stored in an auxiliary memory. Repeated operation requires this memory to be cleared which unavoidably contributes to the energetic cost of error correction. Here, we characterise this contribution for subspace quantum error-correcting codes and identify how it depends on the joint structure of the code, the noise, and the representation of the retained syndrome information. Starting from the Knill-Laflamme conditions, we construct an effective syndrome state whose von Neumann entropy sets a lower bound on the ideal work required to maintain a reusable syndrome register. Projective syndrome readout generally generates additional entropy, and we quantify the resulting gap through measurement inefficiency. We then specialise to stabiliser codes under independent local Pauli noise and analyse two classical levels of syndrome representation. At the level of abstract error labels, degeneracies among single-qubit errors reduce the leading-order entropy of processed recovery labels. At the parity-check level, lower-weight checks reduce the marginal entropy generated by individual measurement outcomes in the low-noise regime. We identify the additional burden associated with retaining and separately erasing these outcomes as a bit-level inefficiency, and illustrate both costs for the five-qubit, Steane, generalised Shor, and rotated surface codes. Our results establish a hierarchy of syndrome-memory energetic costs and identify the code, noise, and measurement structures that control the ideal thermodynamic burden of subspace quantum error correction.

title: Federated Causal Discovery via Regression-Directed Cumulants
abstract: In this paper we study linear non-Gaussian acyclic models (LiNGAM) when used in federated environments. These causal models allow one to go beyond Markov equivalence. However, in many domains data are scarce, and increasing the sample size by centralising data from different clients is not advisable due to regulations such as the GDPR. The federated environment offers an attractive option to balance privacy and causal discovery accuracy. Unfortunately, the standard centralised estimator in the LiNGAM setting, i.e., DirectLiNGAM, cannot be straightforwardly federated. Higher-order cumulant tensors offer a way around this obstacle: they depend only on the joint distribution of the variables involved and add exactly across independent sample groups, so a single communication round suffices in horizontal, vertical, and hybrid partitions. However, FedISHC, i.e., the current federated method along these lines, breaks down under near-symmetric noise. To overcome the above limitation, we introduce the FedRCD family of causal discovery algorithms, and investigate three variants that trade off communication rounds against algebraic noise; two of them are exact federated counterparts of the centralised high-order cumulant (HC) and HC-LiNGAM algorithms, and the single-round variants further effectively support exact unlearning at any granularity, from a single observation to a whole client. Numerical experiments show that at sample sizes typical of real deployments, the entire cumulant-based federated family does not actually rank variables by the population asymmetry that the scores encode at zero. It ranks them by a variance ladder induced by the DAG along its directed paths, the cumulant counterpart of varsortability. Marginal standardisation collapses every cumulant method to near-random ordering, while scale-invariant DirectLiNGAM, not federable under this protocol, is unaffected.

title: A Lower Bound on Energy Cost per Logical-Qubit Operation in Surface-Code Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Surface-code quantum error correction (QEC) is pivotal for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but its energy efficiency remains underexplored. This work derives a practical lower bound on the energy cost per logical-qubit operation, accounting for gate-fidelity decay's impact on code distance and physical-qubit overhead. By modeling the energy consumption of gate operations and error correction, we express the total cost as $ E = (E_g N_g + E_c N_c)/N_l $, where $ E_g $, $ E_c $, $ N_g $, $ N_c $, and $ N_l $ represent gate and physical-qubit energy costs, gate counts, physical-qubit counts, and logical qubit counts, respectively. Gate-fidelity decay increases the required code distance $ d $, scaling $ N_c $ and thus $ E $. We propose normalizing computational cost in joules per logical-qubit operation (JPCUB), isolating logical work from error-correction overhead. Quantitative predictions for $ E_g $, $ E_c $, and $ N_c $ remain [to verify], but the functional dependence on $ d $ and gate fidelities is established. This framework informs energy-efficient QEC design and benchmarks. ## 1. Introduction Surface codes enable fault-tolerant quantum computation by encoding logical qubits in a 2D lattice of physical qubits, correcting errors through syndrome measurements. However, the energy cost per logical operation—critical for scalability—remains poorly quantified. While theoretical foundations exist (Raussendorf & Terhal, 2006; Kitaev, 2003), prior work focuses on error-correction thresholds rather than energy efficiency. Here, we address this gap by deriving a lower bound on energy cost, considering how gate-fidelity decay necessitates larger code distances $ d $, increasing physical-qubit overhead $ N_c $. This analysis connects to the joules-per-compute (JPCUB) benchmark, advocating for energy normalization per logical qubit to disentangle computational work from error-correction costs. ## 2. title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Neural Networks via Genetic Programming
abstract: This paper investigates the limitations of traditional static neural networks in dynamic and unpredictable environments. The core argument is presented: static neural networks lack the inherent flexibility required to adapt effectively to evolving conditions. To address this deficiency, a novel approach is proposed – dynamically reconfigurable neural networks achieved through the application of genetic programming. This methodology leverages evolutionary algorithms to continuously optimize the network's architecture and weight parameters in real-time, responding directly to feedback from the environment. The system's self-reconfiguring capability is demonstrated through a theoretical framework, detailing the core mechanisms and potential benefits. Key components include a fitness function to evaluate network performance, a genetic operator set for architectural and weight modification, and a feedback loop for environmental interaction. The paper outlines the theoretical foundations and provides a roadmap for implementing such a system, highlighting its potential to overcome the rigidity associated with conventional neural network designs. This approach offers a pathway toward more robust and adaptable artificial intelligence systems.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis with Hierarchical Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neuro-symbolic approach to program synthesis, leveraging the strengths of both neural networks and Bayesian Networks within a hierarchical framework. The core challenge in program synthesis, particularly for complex tasks involving hierarchical reasoning, is addressed by combining pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with probabilistic reasoning of Bayesian Networks. The proposed system learns data patterns and simultaneously extracts underlying logical relationships, resulting in the generation of more sophisticated and, crucially, explainable programs. The hierarchical structure allows for the decomposition of complex problems into smaller, more manageable sub-problems, each addressed by a separate level of the Bayesian Network. This approach offers a significant advancement over existing program synthesis techniques by enabling the creation of programs capable of representing and executing intricate, nested logical rules. The system's architecture and learning process are detailed, demonstrating its potential for tackling complex programming challenges where traditional methods fall short.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Causality-Aware Relational Dynamics
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have achieved remarkable success in representing nodes and relationships within graphs for downstream tasks. However, a significant limitation remains when dealing with dynamic graphs, where nodes and their connections evolve over time. Existing methods often treat temporal information as a simple sequence of static graph snapshots, failing to capture the underlying causal dynamics and the sequential dependencies between nodes. This paper introduces a novel temporal graph embedding approach that explicitly incorporates causality and temporal dynamics. We construct a directed acyclic graph (DAG) to represent the causal relationships within the graph, and then utilize a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model the evolution of node embeddings based on this DAG. This methodology allows us to capture the influence of past events on current states while maintaining a structured representation of the graph. The core idea is to leverage the DAG to guide the RNN's state updates, ensuring that the temporal evolution of node embeddings is consistent with the causal structure. The resulting embeddings effectively represent the dynamic behavior of the graph, improving performance in tasks such as node classification and link prediction. The primary contribution is a framework for temporal graph embedding that integrates causality and temporal dynamics, offering a more robust and accurate representation of evolving graph systems.

title: Computational Semantics for Natural Language Understanding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational semantic framework designed to address the challenges of natural language understanding (NLU) by moving beyond traditional symbolic approaches. The core idea is to represent the meaning of natural language sentences using a dynamic logic system augmented with probabilistic reasoning. This allows for the capture of contextual nuances and inference processes inherent in human language comprehension. The framework utilizes dynamic logic to model the evolution of meaning over time and context, while probabilistic reasoning provides a mechanism for handling uncertainty and ambiguity. The system's architecture is described, including key components such as the semantic representation formalism, the inference engine based on dynamic logic, and the probabilistic reasoning module. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to improve NLU tasks, particularly those requiring complex reasoning and contextual understanding. The research contributes a fundamentally different approach to language semantics representation and reasoning.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Computational Traceability
abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in various domains, yet their "black box" nature poses significant challenges to trust, interpretability, and accountability. This research addresses this issue by proposing a novel system for achieving algorithmic transparency through detailed computational traceability. The system meticulously captures and represents the entire execution process of a deep learning model, encompassing intermediate activations, gradient flows during training, and the decision pathways leading to a specific output. This approach moves beyond simple model explanations and provides a granular, verifiable record of the model's internal workings. The core claim is that this level of detail is crucial for fostering trust and facilitating a deeper understanding of these complex systems. The system's architecture is described, along with the key components and their functionalities. Finally, potential applications and future research directions are discussed, highlighting the transformative impact of computational traceability on the field of deep learning.

title: Quantum Neural Networks: Topology Optimization of Neuronal Connections
abstract: This paper investigates the application of topology optimization techniques to enhance the performance of quantum neural networks (QNNs). Traditional QNN architectures often suffer from inefficiencies in information processing due to suboptimal connections between neurons. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing topology optimization algorithms to dynamically adjust the connectivity topology within a QNN, aiming to maximize computational capacity and efficiency. The core claim is that optimizing the neuronal connection topology is a key factor in improving QNN performance. The proposed mechanism involves the iterative application of a topology optimization algorithm, which iteratively modifies the network's connectivity structure based on a defined objective function. The results demonstrate the potential of this method to significantly improve QNN performance, offering a pathway to more powerful and efficient quantum computing architectures. The specific objective function utilized focuses on maximizing the fidelity of quantum state transformations while minimizing the number of connections, representing a novel approach to QNN design. Further exploration will involve investigating different optimization algorithms and network architectures to fully realize the potential of this topology-optimized QNN design.

title: Quantum Privacy Preservation Communication Protocol Based on Quantum Coherence Collapse
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum communication protocol designed for privacy preservation, leveraging the phenomenon of quantum coherence collapse. The core idea is to utilize quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols and strategically introduce coherence collapse operations during transmission, effectively hindering an eavesdropper's ability to access the key. Unlike existing QKD protocols that predominantly rely on quantum entanglement, this approach exploits the unique characteristics of quantum coherence collapse. We outline the protocol's architecture, detailing the key steps involved in key generation and distribution, focusing on the precise implementation of the coherence collapse mechanism. The protocol's security analysis demonstrates its potential to provide robust privacy protection against various eavesdropping attacks. Mathematical formulations are presented to rigorously describe the protocol's operations and security properties. The primary goal is to present a fundamentally different approach to quantum privacy preservation, offering a potentially more secure and efficient solution compared to entanglement-based QKD.

title: Title: Geometric Language for Formalizing Uncertainty in Neural Networks
abstract: Neural networks, while achieving remarkable results, often struggle with uncertainty. Current approaches often rely on approximations and heuristics, which can lead to instability and unreliable predictions. This paper proposes a novel geometric language for formalizing uncertainty within neural networks, aiming to create more robust and reliable models. We introduce a grammar based on Bayesian inference and Monte Carlo simulation, allowing for explicit representation of probabilistic relationships and uncertainty quantification. The core mechanism involves defining a geometric representation of the network's parameters and activations, enabling the construction of probabilistic models and analysis. This approach offers a pathway toward enhanced uncertainty management, potentially leading to improved model generalization and decision-making. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this language through a simplified illustrative example, showcasing its ability to capture and quantify uncertainty in a basic neural network model.

We explore the potential applications of these networks in data compression and material science, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in producing novel fractal structures.

title: L’usage du calcul quantique en finance La perspective d’un institut académique à l’interface entre technologies et usages
abstract: Dans cet article, nous analysons l’impact potentiel du calcul quantique sur la finance du point de vue d’un institut académique positionné à l’interface entre technologies et usages. Nous défendons l’idée que le quantique constitue un bien public, dont les implications dépassent le seul cadre technologique et nécessitent une appropriation par les décideurs économiques. Après avoir souligné l’importance d’une pédagogie adaptée pour rendre ces concepts accessibles aux non-physiciens, nous proposons une taxonomie des principaux algorithmes quantiques pertinents pour la finance : optimisation, algèbre linéaire, Monte Carlo et apprentissage automatique. Ces approches trouvent des applications naturelles dans l’optimisation de portefeuille, la gestion du risque et le pricing de produits dérivés. Enfin, nous mettons en perspective la maturité actuelle du domaine : malgré des avancées significatives, les bénéfices opérationnels restent limités à court terme, tandis que les véritables ruptures sont attendues avec l’émergence de machines quantiques tolérantes aux fautes.

title: A Multi-Indicator Concentration Index for Primary-Care Reimbursement Analytics: Evidence from the Albanian Health-Insurance System
abstract: Background: Public payers must regularly decide which prescribers to look at more closely, with records covering thousands of doctors per quarter and review capacity for only a fraction. How that choice is made bears on equitable access to reimbursed medicines as well as on public funds. Methods: We propose a multi-indicator concentration index scoring each prescriber 0–100 as the sum of nine weighted sub-scores, each measuring the doctor’s deviation from their primary-care centre median on one indicator from the payer’s routine quarterly report; eight are computable from a single quarter. Every score decomposes into named components. The index measures the concentration of indicators above the peer profile, not an estimated probability of misconduct. It is a screening tool for prioritising documentary review. We demonstrate it on one quarter of anonymised data from 335 doctors in 30 Albanian primary-care centres. Results: The eight active sub-scores are mostly weakly correlated (mean |r|=0.28), the two exceptions each pairing a case count with its financial effect. Rankings are robust to alternative weights (Spearman ρ between 0.93 and 0.98), to collapsing those pairs (ρ≥0.98), and to pooling the smallest centres against a shared comparator (ρ=0.95). Against three machine-learning anomaly detectors and two simpler screens, the index selects a different top cohort: doctors whose spending is only moderately raised, but whose new-case and therapy-change counts exceed three times the centre median. In an internal concordance check, two co-author reviewers blinded to the score rated 60 cases sampled partly by index rank; they agreed with each other (Cohen’s κ=0.87, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.00), and the index’s ranking against their consensus gives an AUC of 0.88 (95% CI 0.62 to 0.97). Conclusions: The index gives clinical-administrative reviewers a reproducible, explainable priority order consistent with senior expert judgement on the same indicators. Because no review outcomes are linked to the records and the window is a single quarter, it is supported as a prioritisation tool, not a validated predictor of inappropriate reimbursement; multi-quarter and outcome-linked evaluation are the next steps.
